problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y={(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}+10?$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying a Vertically Shifted Exponential Decay Curve
examples.worked_solution:
First we plot the graph of $y=\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{x}{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/bfe6ffc2b355b488899d29a827f779c60c13ca499312e0425c5b10b07057ed0b.png)

To sketch the graph of $y=\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{x}-3,$ we take the graph of $y=\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{x}$ and shift it $3$ units down. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-2),$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-3.$
